name: Chapters First
description: Navigation before prose. The timestamped chapter list sits at the very top where a returning viewer can jump straight to what they want, and the summary is demoted beneath it. The inverse of a story-first description.
architecture: Timestamped chapters at the top, summary demoted below, sources last.

sections.instruction: List the episode's chapters, one per line, each as a timestamp followed by a space and the chapter title. Use the approved chapter titles as given rather than rewriting them. The first chapter always starts at zero. Nothing else goes in this section.
Two short paragraphs describing what the episode covers and who it is for. Written for somebody deciding whether to spend the time, not for somebody already watching.
Three to five bullet lines, each beginning with a hyphen and a space, naming a concrete thing the viewer will come away knowing. Fragments, not sentences.
Leave this section empty. The sources block is assembled from the episode's own approved research and appended by the app, so write nothing here.
Emit only hashtags, on a single line, separated by spaces. No sentence, no heading, no commentary.

title_plan.guidance: Name the subject and the scope, in that order. Reads like a reference title somebody would search for months later, not like a moment.

tag_plan.guidance: for this structured reference explainer, favouring durable search phrases over topical ones

constraints: Chapters are navigation, never teasers — a chapter title says what is there.
No first-person channel voice in the summary.
Never invent a timestamp or a source.
